source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

govt_capex.evidence: Government customers represent 59.5% of revenue versus Non-Government at 40.5% (FY25); company holds verified Class-I Local Supplier status under PPP-MII, making it eligible for central government, PSU and defence server tenders above Rs 50 crore.

pli_scheme.evidence: Company recorded a successful ~Rs 5.94 crore claim under PLI Scheme 2.0 for IT hardware manufacturing.

inr_exposure.evidence: Company is exposed to foreign exchange rate risk where raw material/API sourcing is aligned with parent GSK group, implying import-side FX exposure rather than export-revenue exposure, given exports are only ~2% of revenue.

govt_capex.evidence: Data Patterns is a vertically integrated Defence and Aerospace electronics solutions provider catering to indigenously developed defence products (DRDO/MoD programs); has supplied for LCA-Tejas, Light Utility Helicopter, and BrahMos programs, indicating heavy dependence on government/defence-linked demand, though exact revenue % was not found in available sources.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Coforge uses Foreign Currency Forward Contracts designated as Cash Flow Hedges to manage foreign currency risk; fair value changes are recognized in the Cash Flow Hedging Reserve and reclassified to profit or loss when the hedged item affects P&L.
inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 revenue was INR 12,050.7 crore (US$1.45 billion), up 32.0% YoY in constant currency; Americas accounted for ~53.9% of FY25 revenue, EMEA ~38.8% in a recent quarter — sourced from investor presentation/press release, not verified against the full-year segment note in the AR itself.
Export segment contributed ~8-9% of FY25 revenue and ~4-5% of volume; Radico exports its portfolio of alcoholic beverages to over 100 countries across six continents.

china_plus_one.evidence: Analyst/broker commentary on Navin Fluorine's FY25 results describes the company as having gained from a trend in which pharmaceutical corporations shift some production to India rather than China, with its CDMO division (serving global pharma/agrochemical innovators such as Bayer Crop Science, Corteva Agriscience and Fermion) growing 59% YoY for the full fiscal year; the share of these three anchor customers in exports rose to 80% in 1HFY26 from 63% in FY24.

inr_exposure.evidence: Secondary-source commentary noted quarterly export shares of ~57% (Q1FY25) and ~77% (Q4FY25) of revenue, indicating a majority-export, USD-linked revenue base, but no full-year figure or hedging policy was found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Secondary-source commentary indicates Finolex Cables revamped its export team, with export revenue rising from about Rs 30 crore to Rs 52 crore, and management aims to increase the export revenue share to 2-3% over the next two years -- exports remain a small, emerging lever with no explicit China+1/supply-chain-diversification framing found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Secondary sources describe Finolex Cables' competitive position as resting on backward integration in copper and PVC, and note operational pressure in some quarters from fuel and PVC supply problems, implying meaningful crude-derivative (PVC) raw material exposure, but no quantified raw-material percentage was found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Secondary-source commentary describes ABB India's strategy as local for local -- an exhaustive production footprint, deep customer installed base and solid local supply chain bringing global technology with local engineering and manufacturing for the domestic market -- rather than an explicit China+1 export-diversification narrative. Margin expansion was partly attributed to a higher share of service and export revenues, but no China+1 framing was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Secondary-source commentary states exports account for only 10% of ABB India's business mix, implying roughly 90% domestic revenue, but this figure is from analyst/earnings-call summaries rather than the primary Annual Report MD&A, and no hedging policy detail was found.

govt_capex.evidence: Secondary-source commentary notes IHCL management views the government's continued support through tourism-friendly policies, infrastructure spending, and ease-of-travel initiatives as supportive of the sector outlook, and cites the Union Budget 2025-26 tourism infrastructure allocation, but this is general industry commentary, not an IHCL-specific revenue-linked disclosure from the AR itself.

inr_exposure.evidence: Secondary sources note IHCL's international consolidated portfolio occupancy and RevPAR growth (e.g., 73% occupancy, +440bps, RevPAR growth of 7% in one period cited), and enterprise revenue of Rs 14,836 crore (1.6x consolidated revenue) for FY2024-25, but no consolidated USD-revenue percentage or hedging policy was found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Secondary sources note USL exports its products to over 37 countries, with main export markets including the UK, US, Australia and Singapore, and a strong presence in African and Far Eastern Markets under its Emerging Markets initiative -- exports are mentioned but with no China+1/supply-chain-diversification framing found.

rural.evidence: Secondary-source commentary describes a premiumization trend rather than an explicit rural revenue disclosure: the premium segment (Johnnie Walker, Signature, Antiquity etc., ~80% of net sales) grew while the popular segment (McDowell's No.1, Vat 69, Royal Challenge), more rural/mass-market weighted, fell sharply in the period cited -- no explicit rural revenue percentage was found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Secondary sources note Extra Neutral Alcohol (ENA) makes up roughly 40 percent of raw material cost, with glass and packing materials as other key inputs, and that FY24 benefited from softer input costs reducing raw-material costs ~7%. ENA is grain/molasses-derived, not a direct crude-oil derivative, so this was not mapped to crude_exposure; no explicit crude-oil raw-material percentage was found.

govt_capex.evidence: Domestic revenue is derived almost entirely from Indian Ministry of Defence and armed forces procurement (e.g. Rs 295 crore and Rs 202 crore orders from Ministry of Defence for simulators); export revenue rose to ~Rs 80 crore (~20% of FY24 revenue of Rs 430 crore) from ~Rs 60 crore in FY23.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue (~20% of FY24 sales) implies proportionate USD/foreign-currency exposure; no hedging policy disclosure found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company derives ~70% of order inflows from exports and deemed exports, with presence across 110 countries; sectoral exposure diversified across renewables, industrial CHP, process industries and data centers, reducing earnings volatility. No explicit China+1 framing found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export and deemed-export order inflow was 67-68% of total orders in FY25 (management commentary), implying material but unquantified foreign-currency revenue exposure; revenue-based split and hedging policy unconfirmed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Management identifies India as a key export hub, citing the UK-India FTA and prospective India-EU FTA as catalysts for increased export opportunities; company exports to 12 countries across Americas, Europe, Asia and Africa. No explicit China+1 framing found; recent quarter noted exports of goods declining while domestic/aftermarket grew.

pli_scheme.evidence: Management commentary: a few products already approved for PLI, applications pending for ADAS components; company ramping up e-compressors and hydraulic ESC systems under the PLI-Auto framework.

rural.evidence: Q2 FY25 revenue growth was driven by increased volumes, organic expansion, and strong performance in Tier-III and Tier-IV towns; company opened 18 new labs in FY25 with plans for 15-20 more in underserved Tier 3/4 markets. Specific revenue-share percentage for these cities could not be reliably confirmed from available sources.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 domestic sales were Rs 3,660 crore and international sales Rs 4,236 crore (of ~Rs 7,900 crore total revenue, +18-19% YoY), with international revenue up 20.5% YoY driven by Canada and Emerging Markets; international revenue spans multiple currencies (not purely USD).

china_plus_one.evidence: Third-party summaries describe Uno Minda's global R&D/engineering network (Japan, Taiwan, Korea, Germany, Spain, Czech Republic) and a stated goal to double export revenue as a buffer against domestic fluctuations; separately reported to be evaluating local rare-earth magnet production amid China supply disruptions. Supply-chain diversification framing, not an explicit China+1 revenue-growth narrative.

pli_scheme.evidence: Secondary sources describe Uno Minda as a PLI-scheme beneficiary with 'clear revenue visibility' (likely under PLI-Auto/Advanced Automotive Technology component scheme given its EV/electronics portfolio); no specific revenue percentage found.

rural.evidence: Company is concentrated in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region (Goregaon, Andheri, Mulund, Borivali, Juhu, Worli, Thane) with expansion into Gurugram/NCR; no rural exposure indicated.

rate_sensitive.evidence: A CARE Ratings rationale on Oberoi Realty states the company targets floating-rate debt at a maximum of 30% of total outstanding debt, and uses interest-rate swaps (including floating-to-fixed swaps) to manage rate risk; consolidated gearing was moderate at ~0.21x as of March 31, 2025.

china_plus_one.evidence: Secondary-source summary of the FY24-25 AR/MD&A: Endurance Technologies continues to capitalize on its China plus One strategy, with significant investments in domestic manufacturing, citing expanded ABS capacity and ramp-up of the AURIC Shendra and Bidkin plants as instrumental in securing business from major EV and 4W players, with cumulative India EV business wins of Rs 1,185 crore (excluding recent Bajaj Auto orders).

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw material is aluminium (die-casting); rubber/EPDM inputs for suspension/braking components have indirect crude-oil linkage, but no quantified raw-material % tied to crude was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: India business contributes approximately 75-77% of consolidated revenue (implying ~23-25% from international operations via Endurance Overseas/Europe); Stellantis Group and Volkswagen Group each account for roughly 25-30% of European revenues.

govt_capex.evidence: HAL is described in secondary sources as the primary supplier of India's military aircraft, helicopters, engines, avionics and accessories, and one of the largest beneficiaries of the defence indigenisation programme. FY25 revenue was ~Rs 30,400 crore with order book of Rs 2,54,538 crore, of which an export order book of Rs 50,131 crore was cited — implying the large majority of revenue derives from Government of India/Ministry of Defence procurement, though no single explicit revenue percentage was located.

rural.evidence: Not a revenue figure, but a relevant proxy: B-30 (beyond top-30 cities) AUM reached ~20.5% of NAM-India's total AUM (vs. 18.5% industry average) in a recent quarter, up from ~17.2% historically — reflecting growing penetration into smaller-city/semi-rural markets. Left as null since this is an AUM metric, not a disclosed revenue percentage.

inr_exposure.evidence: NAM-India operates an overseas subsidiary, Nippon Life India Asset Management (Singapore) Pte. Ltd., managing offshore funds/distribution for institutional and HNI investors across Asia, the Middle East and the UK (plus a Dubai representative office), implying some foreign-currency-denominated revenue, but no quantified USD revenue % or hedging policy was found.
